newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called higher tracking gains on IPE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called higher tracking gains on IPE.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called higher Monday tracking gains in oil futures on London's IPE and placing the oil complex in a technically strong starting point.

"There is no news, so we are following London. But, my feeling is we have made a bottom at the $18.90s, and we are going to test the $19.80 level today," said a New York crude trader. Crude was called up 15 to 20 cents a barrel. Heating oil and gasoline were called up 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.
At 0905 EDT, May Brent was up 19 cents at $18.07 a barrel on the IPE.
Last Thursday, prompt crude confirmed support at $18.96 after hitting that level April 4. It is the lowest point for prompt crude since March 4, 1996.
Last week's highs hovered between 19.70 and $19.90, and dealers said May crude will definitively have to move above $20.00 if it is to maintain its bottom.
"We are going to be choppy from here, but if we don't break above $20.00 in the next three or four sessions, then we will go lower," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc.
Other dealers said the narrowing May/June contango indicates crude is ready to enter an uptrend as the contango was the clearest sign of a crude surfeit which has held crude in its brearish mode.
"The spreads are beginning to hold up, and that is maybe a better sign than anything else," said a New York crude trader.
The May/June contango narrowed to six cents on ACCESS from nine cents Friday and 11 cents Thursday. Contango indicates the nearer contract is cheaper than the later one.
On Friday, May crude settled four cents a barrel lower at $19.53. May gasoline ended off 0.19 cent a gallon at 60.88 cents while May heating oil ended off 0.99 cent at 53.87 cents a gallon.
